## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR renames `--wait` to `--timeout` in the parser, but it doesn't add the `--wait` alias or deprecation warning that its own ADR promises. Any existing caller that passes `--wait` stops working. That needs fixing before merge. The default and format choices are unchanged, as the PR body says.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:6 — correctness — The parser now registers only `--timeout`, so `parse_args(["--wait", "12"])` fails with `error: unrecognized arguments: --wait 12` and `SystemExit(2)`. argparse's prefix matching doesn't help, because `--wait` isn't a prefix of `--timeout`. This contradicts docs/adr/007-timeout.md:5 ("Accept `--wait` as an alias for one release and emit a deprecation warning when it is used"). Could you register `--wait` as a second option string with `dest="timeout"`, or as a separate hidden option that emits a `DeprecationWarning` and sets `timeout`? Please also add tests that `--wait 12` gives `args.timeout == 12` and that the warning is emitted. — Every existing script or caller that passes `--wait` fails as soon as this ships, with no deprecation period, and the decision document added in this PR says something the code doesn't do.

## Important
(none)

(none)

## Strengths
- The timeout default is still 30 (app/cli.py:6), and the `--format` choices `("json", "csv")` with default `"json"` are unchanged (app/cli.py:7). This matches the "Defaults" section of docs/adr/007-timeout.md and the PR body.
- tests/test_cli.py tests the renamed option for the default value, an explicit value, a non-integer value (`--timeout bad`) and a missing value (`--timeout`), and checks for exit code 2.
